item.title: HDFC Bank slips despite Nifty Bank recovery, analysts retain buy ratings
item.description: HDFC Bank fell 2.16 per cent even as banking indices gained, with analysts retaining positive ratings while investors assess the lender's transition under new CEO Anup Bagchi ...
item.dc:creator: Shilpa Rangarajan
item.content:encoded: HDFC Bank shares fell 2.3 per cent on the National Stock Exchange on Monday, just after it named Anup Bagchi, an outsider, as its next managing director and chief executive officer (CEO). The bank became the biggest drag on the Nifty 50, that otherwise rose for the first time in five sessions. HDFC Bank closed at ₹704.80 on the NSE on a day when the Nifty was up 133.80 points or 0.6 per cent at 22,555.75 after a four-session losing streak. Interestingly, HDFC Bank rose 1.5 per cent at ₹731.95 but closed 4 per cent below the day’s high of ₹734.20. It wiped out ₹25,283 crore of market capitalisation. However, even as the markets gave initial thumbs up to Bagchi, investors preferred to wait and watch as the bank is going through a transition. Analysts said Bagchi’s appointment removed a long-running overhang on succession. But traders flagged caution over margins ahead of the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI's) policy decision on October 7, where a 25 basis points (bps) rate increase is widely expected. A Macquarie report says that growth is skewed towards deposits rather than assets under management (AUM) and that its current account savings account (CASA) is also weak. However, brokers also noted a 33 per cent upside potential for the bank's share price in the medium term. The bank has 47 buy ratings and 2 holds, with a 40.1 per cent return potential, according to Bloomberg data. Over the past week, the bank received 14 ‘buy’ ratings and five ‘outperform’ ratings from 21 brokerage firms. Macquarie’s report said HDFC Bank’s Q2FY27 pre-quarter update showed moderate AUM growth of 15.3 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) (up 5.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter or Q-o-Q), trailing peers, while deposits rose 18.8 per cent Y-o-Y (up 4.9 per cent Q-o-Q), boosted by $11.5 billion in foreign currency non-resident (FCNR) inflows. The report added that growth remains skewed towards term deposits, but CASA is weak, as it averaged 10.7 per cent Y-o-Y /1.5 per cent Q-o-Q (₹9.71 trillion in the latest quarter vs ₹9.57 trillion in the previous quarter and ₹8.77 trillion a year ago). The loan-to-deposit ratio eased ₹200 basis points (bps) Y-o-Y but edged up Q-o-Q. Macquarie retains an Outperform rating (target price at ₹875), and added, “while we believe a turnaround in reported performance and a recovery of lost ground will take time, the incoming CEO may have a clear mandate to reinvigorate loan growth, particularly in the retail portfolio, and reclaim deposit market share, with a sharper focus on rebuilding the CASA franchise.” Meanwhile, Nifty Bank closed 0.48 per cent up at 54,714.1, and the benchmark Nifty 50 closed 0.6 per cent up at 22,555.75, while the BSE Bankex closed 0.7 per cent up at 61,788.52, with the broader BSE Sensex closing 0.66 per cent up at 61,788.52. The market recovery in the banking indices were anchored by the 1.63 per cent gains of ICICI Bank and the 4.28 per cent gains of AU Bank, even as HDFC Bank and y Bank dragged the banking indices down. “Overall, I think things are looking alright from here on. Since 2025, concerns around governance and leadership had led to a nearly 30% correction in its market price. Now, with Anup Bagchi taking over as CEO, we expect the bank’s performance to improve as he settles in and gets a better grip on the business. The bank continues to have strong ratings and a solid franchise. So, in my view, it is more a question of time before the improvement starts reflecting in the performance,” said Somil Mehta, head of retail research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan.

item.title: Flipkart invests in TravClan to strengthen international travel offerings
item.description: The investment will strengthen international travel supply, on-ground support and holiday offerings for customers across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel ...
item.dc:creator: Peerzada Abrar
item.content:encoded: E-commerce firm Flipkart has taken a minority stake in TravClan, a global B2B travel tech platform. The investment will strengthen international travel supply and expand the holiday packages available to customers across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel. The companies didn’t reveal the financial details of the deal. Nishant Verman, SVP, corporate development and partnerships, Flipkart, said investing in TravClan strengthens the company’s ability to offer international holiday packages while deepening travel capabilities. “Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Verman. TravClan powers outbound leisure travel with direct supplier listings across domestic and international destinations. Its tech platform enables over 15,000 travel agents to instantly customise and book real-time packages, hotels, and activities, backed by 24/7 on-ground customer support. By integrating TravClan’s partner network, technology and destination operations, Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel can offer customers a wider range of international holiday packages, supported by on-ground assistance. Arun Bagaria, co-founder and CEO, TravClan, said India is becoming one of the largest outbound travel markets in the world, with travellers taking their first international trips driving a significant part of this growth. “The opportunity lies in making these trips more affordable while maintaining reliable service levels. By contracting directly with suppliers and operating our own ground teams, we are able to offer competitive prices and deliver a consistent experience,” said Bagaria. “This partnership with Flipkart allows us to take affordable travel products to millions of Indians as they embark on their international journeys.” The funding will support investment in global supply, technology and destination expansion as TravClan scales its platform and grows its team across business development, engineering and destination operations.

item.title: Jio Platforms likely to launch IPO on October 21, seeks to raise $3.8 bn
item.description: The country's biggest listing to date is Hyundai Motor India's $2.9 billion listing in 2024, while the National Stock Exchange of India made its market debut last month after a $2.3 billion IPO ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms plans to launch its initial public offering on October 21, seeking to raise about $3.8 billion in what is set to be India's biggest listing, two sources familiar with the matter said.The shares are expected to list on October 28.The country's biggest listing to date is Hyundai Motor India's $2.9 billion listing in 2024, while the National Stock Exchange of India made its market debut last month after a $2.3 billion IPO.The sources were not authorised to speak to media and declined to comment. Reliance did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.Proceeds from the offering will largely be used to repay debt owed by its telecoms division. Jio Platforms, which counts Meta and Google among its major foreign investors, also runs AI, cloud and enterprise network businesses.India has seen a rush of companies coming to market, with proceeds raised during April to September this year marking a record for the period.Furthermore, almost 250 companies are in the pipeline to raise a combined 4.65 trillion rupees ($48 billion) through IPOs, according to information provider PRIME Database. This includes Danish brewer Carlsberg's India business, and hotel aggregator Oyo's parent Prism. 4 new market debuts disappoint despite broader recoveryAll the new listings that debuted on the bourses on Monday closed at discounts to their issue prices, signalling weak investor confidence even as the broader market showed signs of recovery after an eight-week losing streak. German Green Steel and Power listed at ₹128.20 (down 7.7 per cent from its ₹139 issue price), Runwal Enterprises at ₹298.95 (about 1.98 per cent below its ₹305 issue price), and Snapdeal parent Acevector at ₹26.1 (18.44 per cent below its ₹32 issue price). Meanwhile, Orient Cables closed 48 per cent higher at ₹403.30- Our bureau Jane Street denies market manipulation in court  Jane Street Group denied charges of manipulation as it mounted its defense against the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) telling a local court that stocks in a banking index fell or rose irrespective of its trading activity. The Wall Street firm sought redacted counterparty infor­mation included in Sebi’s trade logs that formed part of the regulator’s July interim order. Jane Street's appeal is a test case of Sebi's authority after 2025 order against the firm and seizure of alleged ill-gotten gains of ₹48.4 billion. - Agencies

item.title: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to testify at NYC hearing on AI
item.description: Coxon will appear at request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around technology ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Nacha Cattan and Laura Nahmias Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that artificial intelligence could become too powerful for humans to control, will testify Monday at a New York City Council hearing alongside representatives of some of the world’s biggest AI companies.  Coxon will appear at the request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around the technology, according to people familiar with the matter.  Coxon quit Anthropic last month and issued a stark warning about the race to develop increasingly powerful AI, accusing his former employer and OpenAI of “gambling with our lives.” He confirmed he plans to testify on Monday. The hearing will put some of the industry’s most vocal critics in the same room as representatives of Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Meta Platforms Inc.  Former Google DeepMind researcher Alex Turner and Daniel Kokotajlo, executive director of the AI Futures Project and a former OpenAI researcher, are also expected to testify, according to one of the people. The four major AI companies will send policy and safety officials, the person said.  Turner confirmed he plans to attend the hearing. A spokesperson for Google declined to comment. Kokotajlo and representatives of the other companies didn’t respond to requests for comment. The hearing is part of an effort by New York officials to play a larger role in regulating an industry that has expanded rapidly in the city even as much of AI regulation remains the province of federal and state governments. One proposal before the council, sponsored by Menin, would give whistleblowers a portion of fines or penalties recovered from AI companies following reported violations. Other legislation under consideration would allow people harmed by AI systems to sue developers under certain circumstances and require third-party validation of some systems before they can be deployed in the city. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google agreed to appear after Menin’s office warned that they could be subpoenaed, while Meta had committed to attending earlier, Bloomberg News previously reported. The Council subpoenaed SpaceX’s artificial intelligence unit after it failed to respond to requests to appear.
